messages:
maya: Heads-up — noticed a cohort of tenant invoices where the invoice token total is ~2-5% lower than the metering dashboard for the same window. Not a big money gap but noisy for customers. Anyone else seeing this?
liam: Yep saw a spike yesterday around 17:00 UTC. Guessing late session-end events?
zara: I dug a bit — most mismatches correlate with edge proxies returning session_end events after the ingestion watermark. The ingest pipeline currently stamps events into hourly buckets based on arrival watermark, then we dedupe by session id. Late session_end moves tokens into previous bucket -> ledger reconciliation drops them in preview.
aj: Can you paste an example event flow?
zara: Sure. Simplified: 1) session_start @16:45 (tokens accumulate) 2) session_end @17:05 (arrives at ingestion at 17:12 due to edge retry) 3) ingestion assigns it to 17:00 bucket because watermark=17:00 4) accumulator already finalized 17:00 window and did fold with optimistic dedupe -> session_end ignored by finalizer.
sam: Oof. So finalizer is using arrival-time bucket plus an optimistic closed flag. We need either a grace window or a different watermarking strategy.
liam: I worry about unbounded grace windows — increases memory and could let a noisy tenant push our finalization back. Maybe per-tenant adaptive grace?
maya: Customer-facing ask: console invoice preview should be stable. If we delay finalization, invoices lag. If we finalize early we undercount. Balance needed.
aj: What about moving sessionization to use event timestamps (source-time) + ingestion-side reorder buffer keyed by session id, then finalize by last-seen-timestamp per-session instead of strict hourly cut?
zara: That reduces late-arrival loss but complicates cross-session aggregation and increases state footprint. Also, event timestamps from some proxies are flaky.
liam: Another option: keep current hourly finalizer but emit a late_adjustment event pipeline that can patch invoices when late session_end arrives within N hours. This way preview remains fast and we reconcile later. We already have adjustments for promo credits; reuse?
billing-bot: billing-service: created adjustment record tenant=t-431 delta=+342 tokens reason="late-session-end" (source_event_id=evt_987654321)
sam: If we go adjustments route we need strong telemetry to surface when an invoice had adjustments — console should surface a timeline so customers understand line-item churn. Also analytics needs to know adjusted vs canonical.
maya: Agree. UX: add a badge "reconciled" on invoice rows with hover that shows adjustments and a small graph of token inflow over time.
liam: Implementation plan suggestion: (A) Emit late_adjustment events when session_end hits after finalization but within 24h; (B) Add route_trace_id and session_id to all billing events for traceability; (C) Console: show adjustments timeline and an "adjusted_tokens" column; (D) Telemetry: add gauge metric metering.adjustments.count and histogram metering.adjustment_lag_seconds.
aj: For (A) do we want 24h default? Might be long. Maybe start with 6h and monitor. We can make configurable per-tenant.
zara: Also need a dedupe improvement: when adjustment arrives, ensure idempotent application using event_id. We currently dedupe by (session_id, bucket) only which is insufficient.
liam: Right. Add event_id idempotency key and store last_applied_event per-session in the accumulator store (ttl 48h). Cost estimate low for per-session small key.
sam: Ops concern: monitoring noise — dashboards should show adjustment rate and top offending tenants so we can contact integrators.
maya: Can we add a console flag for customers: "prefer eventual accuracy (allow late adjustments)" vs "prefer stable preview (no late adjustments)" — defaults to eventual accuracy.
liam: Nice. We should also create an alert if adjustments_rate > 0.5% of tokens over rolling 24h for the prod cluster.
aj: I'll draft a small RFC with sequence diagrams and storage implications. Plan to spike a PoC: late_adjustment emitter + idempotency patch.
zara: I'll run a sampling job to tag examples where session_end arrival > finalizer_time and collect tenant metadata.
billing-bot: billing-service: emitted metric metering.adjustments.count=1 tenant=t-431 lag_seconds=420
maya: Thanks. Next steps: aj + liam + zara to pair on PoC, sam to design dashboard tiles, i'll mock console UX. Follow-up sync Friday 15:00 UTC? :thumbsup:
